title: Reading Drill — Designing an Easy-to-read Timetable
description: One short passage, five questions. Recommended time: 8 minutes.

passages.title: Designing an Easy-to-read Timetable
passages.body:
**A** A community bus used a folded timetable with all routes printed on one sheet. A transport group watched people unfold the sheet and noted which panels they opened first.

**B** The first redesign put the most-used route on the outside. It also placed the first and last departures in bold type so people in a hurry could find them easily.

**C** Low-vision readers tested a second edition with fewer columns and wider line spacing. Weekend services remained on a separate panel to prevent weekday departures being mistaken for Sunday times.

questions.prompt: A transport group watched people unfold the sheet and noted which ______ they opened first.
questions.instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage.
questions.explanation: A transport group watched people unfold the sheet and noted which panels they opened first.

questions.prompt: It also placed the first and last departures in ______ so people in a hurry could find them easily.
questions.instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage.
questions.explanation: It also placed the first and last departures in bold type so people in a hurry could find them easily.

questions.prompt: Weekend services remained on a separate ______ to prevent weekday departures being mistaken for Sunday times.
questions.instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage.
questions.explanation: Weekend services remained on a separate panel to prevent weekday departures being mistaken for Sunday times.

questions.prompt: Departure times were spaced farther apart in a later edition.
questions.instructions: Does this statement agree with the information in the passage?
questions.explanation: Low-vision readers tested a second edition with fewer columns and wider line spacing. Weekend services remained on a separate panel to prevent weekday departures being mistaken for Sunday times.

questions.explanation: The first redesign put the most-used route on the outside. It also placed the first and last departures in bold type so people in a hurry could find them easily.
